key_insight: ACCT lets different-sized LLMs within the same model family reuse context computation by converting a source model’s KV cache into sparse KV states for a target model.
engineering_relevance: Heterogeneous LLM deployments could reduce repeated context-processing costs when switching models without requiring the target to prefill the original context.
method: Cartographer selects query-relevant context tokens for each target layer and KV head.
Allocator distributes a shared KV token budget across target layers and heads.
Compiler transforms selected source KV entries into target-compatible sparse KV states.
evidence_signal: Across five general-capability benchmarks and six context-dependent tasks, ACCT matched or exceeded target-model performance with 75% smaller KV caches; at approximately 19K context tokens, KV conversion was 6.5–21.2× faster than target context prefill.
watch_item: Results cover different-sized models within the same family; compatibility across model families and end-to-end deployment gains remain unestablished by the abstract.
